overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals clear audience preference for extreme space anomalies, bizarre planetary physics, and high-stakes 'What If' scenarios. Recent uploads focused on extreme exoplanets and cosmic phenomena (e.g., IYuce8vaU3Y 'Liquid Diamond Planet', A9Qa-RmuOr0 'Venus Day Longer Than Year', v1rrcZLdp4U 'Planet Darker Than Coal') are capturing significantly higher views-per-day and engagement (likes/comments-per-view) compared to older psychological or minor biological facts. Space-based conceptual curiosities drive the highest retention and engagement loops for FACTVERSE.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) with 1,028 views and 38 likes, and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) with 1,027 views and 36 likes outperform generic facts significantly.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on surreal astronomical worlds and strange physical laws governing distant planets.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring 'What If You Fell Into...' generate higher curiosity-driven engagement loops, averaging over 35+ likes per short compared to passive descriptive titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame space and science facts as direct second-person experiential scenarios ('What If You...') to maximize initial hook retention.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, 5 views) and songs stuck in your head (Jc04LVKNd2s, 17 views) showed very low velocity and stagnant engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological tricks unless paired with a high-contrast physical threat or extreme paradox.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos relying solely on standard descriptive statements without an existential or mind-bending twist underperform across views-per-day metrics.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate flat statements; every title must introduce a paradox, extreme scale, or counter-intuitive reality.
